newsitem.title: INDIA: Polling begins in Kashmir elections.
newsitem.headline: Polling begins in Kashmir elections.

text.p: Polls opened in the Himalayan region of Kashmir on Saturday for the election of its first state assembly since militants launched a separatist rebellion six years ago, Indian officials said.
Polling stations in 26 of 87 constituencies in Jammu and Kashmir state opened at 7.00 a.m. (0130 GMT) and were scheduled to close at 5.00 p.m. (1130 GMT). The weather was overcast.
Around 1.3 million of the state's 4.5 million voters were eligible to cast ballots.
Voting in remaining constituencies will take place on September 16, 21 and 30 to enable election officials and some 200,000 security personnel to move between regions.
Final results were expected in early October.
The last state assembly was elected in 1987 amid widespread allegations of rigging.
It was dissolved in 1990 to allow New Delhi to impose direct rule and move thousands of paramilitary troops into the state to try to quell an insurgency in which more than 20,000 people have died.
Dozens of militant groups are fighting for either independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan, which New Delhi accuses of arming and training guerrillas.
Islamabad says it offers only moral and diplomatic backing.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left government hopes the restoration of democracy will help end militancy and revive the economy of the only Moslem majority state in mostly Hindu India.

Some guerrilla groups have threatened to disrupt the polls, being held four months after general elections that were marred by allegations security forces and pro-government militants coerced some people into voting. Authorities denied the charges.
